solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Vigorously march with pride to end of avenue — and this? (13, three words)

definitions.text: Vigorously march with pride to end of avenue — and this?

indicators.note: doing something vigorously throws everything about, so the following words are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Troops parade proudly to the end of a grand boulevard, and the clue asks what stands there.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a victory parade marches down the Champs-Élysées to the Arc de Triomphe at the avenue's end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris monument stands at the top of the Champs-Élysées, the destination of triumphal parades down that avenue.

clue.text: Bit of publicity shifting No. 1 in pop revival

indicators.note: shifting something means moving it away, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: a promo is a short promotional item

indicators.note: number one in a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A publicity snippet changes its lead act in a pop music revival.
explanation.walkthrough: Romo was a short-lived 1990s British revival of New Romantic pop styles.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a mid-1990s music and fashion movement that brought back the New Romantic look, so a revival.

clue.text: What can create diphthong like this turns up when 'headland' is inscribed

indicators.note: something inscribed is written inside, so this word goes within the other
in a down entry, turning up reads the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, so
ras is a headland or cape

explanation.surface: A phonetics note about how a diphthong forms, with a quoted word slotted in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like this' is the Latin word editors print after a quoted slip; the headland is the Arabic-derived word seen in place names such as Ras Tanura.
explanation.definitionFit: Crasis is the fusing of two vowels at a word boundary into one long vowel or diphthong, as in Greek.

clue.text: Led astray, I dispatched beam inwardly, once void of lights?

indicators.note: inwardly says the following pieces sit inside the scrambled word
led astray means sent off course, so these letters wander out of order

parts.note: taken as written, then scrambled
taken as written
dispatched means sent
a beam of light is a ray

explanation.surface: A confession: misled, I sent a beam inside something once dark.
explanation.walkthrough: Lights are lungs, as in offal, so to be emptied of lights is to be disembowelled; 'once' marks the Spenserian spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Spenser's verb means to disembowel, and removing the lights, an old word for lungs, is gutting a carcass.

clue.text: Source of cuppas: move round holding running water (6, two words)

indicators.note: holding something means having it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to turn is to move round
ea is a dialect word for a river or running water

explanation.surface: Advice on making tea: swirl the pot around with hot water from the tap.
explanation.definitionFit: A large heated container dispenses hot water for brewing many cups at once, as at a church fete.

clue.text: Tunic cut short from below, cause to change planes?

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from below runs the letters upwards
cutting something short trims off its last letter

parts.note: a tabard is a sleeveless tunic

explanation.surface: A tunic is shortened at the hem, and somehow this makes someone switch aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Planes' suggests aircraft, but this is geometry: to rabat is to rotate one plane about a line until it lies in another.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry the verb means to turn a plane about its line of intersection until it coincides with another plane.

clue.text: Parts of shaft getting switched? Opposite of ease resulting

indicators.note: naming the parts tells you the word is split in two before they move
switching the parts swaps the two halves of the word round

parts.note: a thill is the shaft of a cart

explanation.surface: Pieces of a shaft get swapped, and the opposite of comfort follows.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: Ruskin's coinage is the counterpart of wealth, meaning ill-being, so 'opposite of ease' points at its misery.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruskin coined the word as the opposite of wealth: misery and ill-being, the reverse of comfort and wellbeing.

clue.text: Mum tucked into rather large drink, just as our forebears did (11, two words)

indicators.note: something tucked into another is placed inside it

parts.note: more in the sense of rather, sooner
ma is an informal word for mother
a jorum is a large drinking bowl or its contents

explanation.surface: Mother is hidden in a hefty drink, the way the old folk always took it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means after the manner of our ancestors, doing things the traditional way.

clue.text: Scheme noisy gent abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned means left behind, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: plangent means loud and resounding
taken as written; these letters go

explanation.surface: A scheme whereby a loud man is left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean an arranged programme of action, a synonym pair as nouns.

clue.text: Legatee of female with attractive quality, and gold

parts.note: her as the possessive of she
it is sex appeal
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: An heir to a charming woman's fortune and her gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A heritor is one who inherits, the same as someone receiving a legacy under a will.

clue.text: Folly? I'll have one to rear of grand house, not Anglo-Norman

indicators.note: placed at the rear means coming after the other piece
not having something means those letters are taken out

parts.note: a manor is a grand country house
AN is the abbreviation for Anglo-Norman
taken as written
a means one

explanation.surface: Someone wants a folly put up behind a stately home, but not a Norman-style one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Folly' suggests a garden ornament beside the grand house, but it means foolishness.
explanation.definitionFit: Moria is a rare word for foolishness or stupidity, taken from the Greek for folly.

clue.text: Hen harrier, unusually harsh, tucked into maggot (9, two words)

indicators.note: tucked into means placed inside the other word

parts.note: mawk is a dialect word for maggot

indicators.note: unusually means not in the usual way, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird of prey, unusually fierce, swallowing a grub.
explanation.definitionFit: The North American name for the hen harrier, a raptor that hunts low over marshland.

clue.text: Landing fish with end of catcher

parts.note: the sole is a flatfish

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: An angler lands a fish at the end of the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Landing' looks like hauling in a catch; it is a noun for a raised floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A soler is an old word for an upper room or loft, a raised floor level like a landing.

clue.text: Vagabonds smuggle stones (semi-precious)

parts.note: to run goods is to smuggle them
agates are semi-precious stones

explanation.surface: Wandering rogues sneak gemstones past customs.
explanation.definitionFit: A runagate is an archaic word for a runaway or wanderer, a vagabond drifting without home.

clue.text: With power to gather in piles, albe crookedly, master pocketed

definitions.text: With power to gather in piles

indicators.note: something pocketed is put inside, here within the other letters
crookedly means not straight, so these letters are bent out of order

parts.note: an archaic word for although, taken as written
massa is a dialect form of master

explanation.surface: Something able to heap things up, though a bit lopsidedly, once a boss is enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to accumulate in heaps, so the adjective means capable of being heaped together.

clue.text: Poet's botch, omitting rain from stanza

indicators.note: omitting means leaving out, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a quatrain is a four-line stanza
taken as written; these letters go

explanation.surface: A poet's clumsy draft drops the weather from a verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet's' signals Shakespeare's usage; 'botch' here is an old word for a boil or pimple, not a bungled job.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare used the word for a pimple or boil, which a botch also meant in older English.

clue.text: Time for vigil, avoiding e.g. poisonous stuff

indicators.note: avoiding means keeping away from, so those letters are left out

parts.note: a vigil is kept through the evening and night
taken as written; these letters go

explanation.surface: A night watch steers clear of something toxic.
explanation.definitionFit: Venin is a toxic substance found in snake venom, a technical term for a poison.

clue.text: Mouse trapped by mesh in error

indicators.note: something trapped by the words is held inside them, spanning their letters

parts.note: run across the end of mesh, the whole of in and the start of error

explanation.surface: A mouse is caught in a net by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouse' looks like the rodent in the trap, but it is slang for a black eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang for a black eye, the bruise round the eye after a punch.

clue.text: Having run in eliminating round, almost finish? Buck up!

indicators.note: the round has the next piece inside it

parts.note: a heat is a qualifying round of a race
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: almost means not quite, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: end means finish

explanation.surface: An athlete scrapes through a qualifier and is told to cheer up.
explanation.definitionFit: To buck up someone is to encourage them, the same as to give them heart.

clue.text: Cheers welcoming fringe melodies?

indicators.note: welcoming someone means taking them in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ta-ta is goodbye, as cheers can be
a hem is an edge or border

explanation.surface: An audience applauds tunes from the festival fringe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' reads as applause, but it is the British farewell, like ta-ta.
explanation.definitionFit: Themata is the plural of thema, a theme, and musical themes are melodies; the question mark admits the stretch.

clue.text: Like a post, completely ordinary, fastened badly at the edges

indicators.note: letters at the edges sit either side of the other piece, wrapping it
done badly means done wrongly, so these letters come out in a muddled order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
O is the abbreviation for ordinary

explanation.surface: A fence post, quite plain and badly fixed along its sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As deaf as a post' is the idiom behind 'Like a post'; 'completely' adds the degree.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'deaf as a post' compares total inability to hear with a post's insensibility, and stone- means utterly.

clue.text: Angler's has a long handle — gutted pollan goes into food selection

indicators.note: goes into means is placed inside the other piece

parts.note: a diet is a chosen range of food

indicators.note: a gutted fish has its insides removed, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: An angler cleans a pollan, an Irish freshwater fish, and adds it to a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dip net is a small net on a long pole, used by anglers for scooping up fish.

clue.text: Fellow, one admitting faulty clue, yielding grounds

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the other piece goes inside
something faulty is not right, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
a means one
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A man confesses to a bad clue and so gives his reasons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounds' reads as reasons, but it means dregs or sediment.
explanation.definitionFit: Fecula is sediment or starchy deposit settling from a liquid, which is what coffee grounds are.

clue.text: Song before party's introduced by H. Styles

indicators.note: introduced by means the other piece comes first

parts.note: taken as written
an air is a song or tune
a do is a party; the 's makes it DOS

explanation.surface: A track that precedes a party, presented by the pop singer Harry Styles.
explanation.walkthrough: H. Styles reads as the singer's name, but H is a piece and Styles the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairdos are hairstyles, so the plural styles in the sense of ways of arranging hair.

clue.text: Money needed when centre of routine is moved to the fore

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter, the one that moves
moved to the fore means shifted to the front of the word

parts.note: a chore is a routine task

explanation.surface: Cash is required when the heart of a daily schedule gets brought forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Money' looks like a modern word for cash, but this is old slang, from the gold colour of coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is old slang for money, especially gold coin, from its yellow colour.

clue.text: Toadies locally requiring approval in appeal for help

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal
OK signals approval

explanation.surface: Local yes-men want endorsement when someone calls for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locally' marks a dialect word: sook is Scots and Northern English for a sycophant or crybaby.
explanation.definitionFit: In dialect a sook is a fawning person, a sycophant, so the plural matches flatterers.

clue.text: Foreign bread requiring a long time following order without being warm

indicators.note: following means coming after the other piece
without means lacking, so those letters are removed

parts.note: an injunction is a court order
unction is warmth or fervour of manner; these letters go
an era is a long period

explanation.surface: Baking foreign bread takes ages after an order to leave it unheated.
explanation.definitionFit: Injera is the spongy sourdough flatbread of Ethiopia and Eritrea, so a bread from abroad.

clue.text: Timber tree yielding oil, not quite enough for oil lamp

indicators.note: not quite enough means falling one short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: an Argand is a kind of oil lamp with a tubular wick

explanation.surface: A tree giving oil, but not enough to fill a lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: The argan is a Moroccan tree with hard timber whose kernels give a prized oil.

clue.text: Sort tax

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to sort an animal is to neuter it
second meaning: an old English land tax paid to the crown

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks you to organise taxes; the first word is the informal sense of neutering, as in 'get the cat sorted'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means castrate, informally to sort; as a noun it is the Anglo-Saxon tax or tribute.

clue.text: Force brake by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it means judged by how a word is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: a brake is a thicket, as is a copse

explanation.surface: Applying the brakes forcefully, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brake' looks like the car pedal, but it is a clump of bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: The police force is collectively the cops, slang for police officers.

clue.text: Bit of old salad? Her leaves showing incipient decay

indicators.note: leaves means goes away from, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a blether is a spell of rambling talk, a jumble of words likened to a salad; the word is Scots
taken as written; these letters go

explanation.surface: A bit of stale salad: her lettuce leaves are starting to go off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as lettuce leaves in the salad, but it is the verb for departing.
explanation.definitionFit: Blet is the soft, overripe state of fruit like medlars just before it rots, the beginning of decay.

clue.text: Granular item stirring under loch

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something gritty moving beneath a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A chondrule is a small round grain found embedded in stony meteorites, a tiny granule.

clue.text: Top pipe requiring something to tune round lines?

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a key tunes a piano or tightens a string peg
L is line, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A first-rate pipe needs a tuning key fitted around its lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top pipe' reads as the finest pipe; in drilling the kelly is the topmost length of pipe, which the rotary table turns.
explanation.definitionFit: In oil drilling the kelly is the uppermost square section of drill pipe, driven by the rotary table.

clue.text: Birds leaving Luxembourg for Spain, red of coat

indicators.note: one letter leaving for another means it is swapped out for the second

parts.note: gulls are seabirds
L is the international car code for Luxembourg
E is the international car code for Spain

explanation.surface: Birds fly from Luxembourg to Spain, with a coat of red feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: One L of GULLS becomes E. 'Coat' is a coat of arms, not plumage.
explanation.definitionFit: Gules is the heraldic term for the colour red on a coat of arms.

clue.text: Marry — after it endures shakily, a miscalculation

indicators.note: after means this piece comes second
something done shakily is unsteady, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
to mate is to pair up or marry

explanation.surface: Getting married once the relationship has wobbled along is a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: An underestimate is a judgement that falls short of the true amount, one kind of error in reckoning.
